text:
Ethan: hey folks, first day hiccup. Im at home with a router that does automatic LTE failover. VPN connects and ssh to bastion works initially, but whenever my ISP link flaps to LTE the ssh sessions drop and docker pulls from the internal registry hang. traceroute shows different public IPs when it flips. anyone seen asymmetric NAT/failover + vpn issues?

Priya: welcome Ethan! yep thats classic asymmetric routing / SNAT change on failover. When your source IP changes mid-TCP flow the state on the VPN/edge will not match and packets get dropped. Two quick checks: reproduce with `ping -M do -s 1400 <bastion_ip>` to see MTU issues, and run `ssh -v bastion` to watch when the TCP connection resets.

Ethan: I ran `ssh -v` and it shows connection reset by peer right after the failover. MTU seemed fine but the public IP changed.

Nate: if your router changes the source IP, there are a few approaches: 1) avoid link-level failover while on VPN (disable automatic failover during work sessions), 2) use a VPN client that supports binding to a specific interface + rekeying to preserve session, 3) run `autossh` with quick reconnects and `ServerAliveInterval` so workflows recover gracefully.

Ethan: option 1 is doable but Id like to keep LTE on for redundancy. what about sticky NAT on the edge so the VPN keeps the session?

Priya: we can look into session affinity / sticky SNAT on the VPN terminator, but that has tradeoffs. For mobile/failover devices it's tricky because public IPs legitimately change. We usually recommend: a) keep long-lived connections over a TLS-based web-bastion (websocket/HTTP) which is more tolerant of client IP changes, or b) configure SSH to reconnect transparently using `ProxyCommand` + `socat` or `sshuttle`.

Ethan: web-bastion sounds promising. is it suitable for docker registry traffic too?

Nate: web-bastion is SSH-in-browser only. For registry/other TCP you can either use an authenticated dev-proxy that speaks HTTPS (we have `dev-proxy.redwood.internal`), or set up a local SSH tunnel that autossh recreates when the WAN changes: `autossh -M 0 -f -N -L 5000:internal.registry.redwood:5000 bastion` and configure Docker to use that local port. That way when autossh reconnects, the tunnel re-establishes.

Ethan: autossh + local tunnel worked when I simulated disconnection, but theres a brief window where pulls fail until reconnect. Any way to make it seamless?

Priya: you can use `socat` + `ssh` with a tiny HA proxy locally that retries connections, or use `ssh -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes` so you don't get half-broken tunnels. For true seamlessness you'd need the infra side to accept the new src IP and keep the session state synchronized which is not trivial.

Ethan: would changing KeepAlives help avoid reset during NAT change?

Nate: KeepAlives help detect dead peers faster and may reduce the time you wait before reconnects, but they won't stop resets if the NAT mapping is gone. Also consider adding `IPQoS 0x00`/`IPQoS af11` in `~/.ssh/config` to avoid weird QoS drops on network changes.

Support-bot: Note: onboarding docs include a "Mobile/failover networks" section with autossh and web-bastion tips. https://redwood.internal/onboard/networks (automated)

Ethan: nice. two asks: 1) can infra evaluate adding a short-term edge rule to allow new SNAT addresses for a reconnect window? 2) can we add an autossh example to onboarding?

Priya: please open a ticket in #infra with your router model, public IP samples and a pcap if you can. Well evaluate an edge-side reconnect window (might be INFRA-5200-level work). Ill add an autossh snippet to the onboarding doc now.

Infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-5200 "Investigate client IP changes during consumer WAN failover and reconnect behavior" (https://redwood.internal/infra/5200)

Ethan: thanks everyone, autossh + local dev-proxy is a good stopgap. saving these notes to my checklist. :thumbsup:
